selection: One common subset minimizes equal-corpus, equal-encoder-seed mean discovery EER. Start at all 36 phones; evaluate every one-phone addition/deletion, accept the strict best improvement. At a single-move plateau (or single-move budget exhausted), evaluate every one-for-one swap. Resume single moves after an accepted swap. At most 8 single moves and 2 swaps. Ties between improving candidates use inventory order; no equal-score moves. This bounded local search is not exhaustive.
partition: Hash-sort validation speaker IDs separately within each corpus; first ceil(n/2) are discovery, remainder confirmation. Both query and claimed speaker must belong to the same partition. All enrollment audio, original masks and per-phone intervals are fixed. Only normal verification is used in search.
support: Keep at least one of a/i/u/e/o to guarantee identical score availability under the existing five-vowel eligibility gate. Every vowel can be removed individually. Original universally-registered-phone masks remain fixed across candidates and claims. No newly scorable queries are added.
confirmation: Freeze the single discovery winner before opening confirmation scores. Report confirmation once, without revising the subset or search. These speakers were already used for the original Transformer checkpoint selection; this is held out only from the new subset search, not independent model development.
evaluation: Freeze winner and all full-validation FAR1% thresholds before reading test arrays. Evaluate only all36 and the one winner on the same original test trials, including JVS cross-text secondary. Recompute Transformer attention and softmax for every mask. No encoder or fusion retraining, checkpoint changes or test-driven changes.
limits: Previously observed test cohorts. Three acoustic seeds, one Transformer seed. No new speakers or recordings. Original intervals are fixed but used audio duration decreases with selection, so this is not a fixed-duration comparison. Paired speaker bootstrap conditions on the selected subset and fixed models and excludes search/training uncertainty. Confirmation does not gate or change which candidate is tested.
